correctness.rationale: All Latin-square quantifiers and ranges are explicit. The rook subcomplex has nerve K_{n,n}; replacement triangles give π1 surjectivity. Every rectangular generator bounds either two triangles or the verified six-triangle embedded disk, proving trivial π1 (not just zero H1). The exact rank and vanishing outside H2 over every field follow from Cioabă–Mim, arXiv:2606.27328 Theorem 3.12, independently checked in relevant sections; universal coefficients give integral Z-free H2, and Hurewicz plus homology Whitehead gives the full wedge type. Packaged standalone finite checker returned VERIFY_OK on four group-derived Latin squares (including two nonisomorphic order-six tables), with independently enumerated maximal cliques and mod-2 ranks; this supplements the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The exact-object June 2026 primary paper establishes all-field homology and explicitly lists the six triangular faces as a signed two-chain, but does not assert or prove trivial π1, a disk filling, or the final homotopy equivalence. These topological conclusions are not consequences of homology vanishing alone. A restricted earlier odd-cyclic homotopy result lacks all even orders and all nongroup Latin squares; the new proof is genuinely uniform in the Latin condition. Bounded indexed-record and literature searches found no broader dominating theorem. The possibility of an implicit/unindexed full-domain equivalence is recorded as a substantive residual risk.
residual_risks: The six triangle set is written down in the 2026 homology paper; an implicit geometric interpretation may already be known or treated there as immediate.
An equivalent full-domain homotopy proof in unindexed or inaccessible literature cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: A complete natural infinite-family homotopy classification for all Latin squares is a structural invariant strictly beyond the known all-field Betti tables and beyond the earlier odd cyclic subfamily. The six-triangle embedded-disk lemma proves vanishing of the actual nonabelian fundamental group, a generally nontrivial issue even when H1 vanishes. The theorem distinguishes nonisomorphic order-six Latin squares via their sphere counts (116 for Z6, 98 for S3) and handles arbitrary quasigroups without algebraic restrictions. No equivariant or chosen homology basis is asserted.
